## Wave 14 compact integration and acceptance packet — Regional Supply And Travel

The wave remains a documentation-only proposal over **route exchange and stewardship**. Before implementation, verify the source owner, stable IDs, consumer, state ladder, host route, save section, replay fixture, accessibility behavior, performance budget, and rollback. The high-volume bank must pass a representative sample before expansion. Story branches must change a reachable owner state or projection and retain a coherent refusal path. Any missing seam, duplicate authority, unowned mechanic, or contradictory save contract stops the packet and returns it to premise review.

**Five-point handoff:** (1) current-source premise and collision search; (2) one owner and one event/save seam; (3) data, localization, migration, and validator evidence; (4) player route, side-quest callback, replay, accessibility, and performance evidence; (5) exact files, focused verification, limitations, rollback, and next audit.

## Continuation Wave 15 — Plan 5 — Regional Supply And Travel

Wave 15 adds a fresh, owner-bound expansion layer for **regional supply and travel**. It is a planning scaffold only. The current 30-field structure remains active; these passes add new playable seams, high-volume authoring, story callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **route, cargo, settlement, weather, vehicle, communications, and expedition owners**. Material anchors include **a stamped arrival slip, a shared blanket, a driver’s raised palm, and a route card dated in pencil**. Observable markers include **arrival confidence, sharing window, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and correction history**.

### Pass 144 — Arrival Evidence Cards

This pass tests how **arrival evidence cards** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over route, cargo, settlement, weather, vehicle, communications, and expedition owners; it does not add a second regional supply and travel authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Arrival Evidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees arrival confidence, sharing window, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and correction history with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Arrival Evidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Arrival Evidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Arrival Evidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present arrival confidence, sharing window, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and correction history as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Arrival Evidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross arrival confidence, sharing window, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and correction history with the material anchors a stamped arrival slip, a shared blanket, a driver’s raised palm, and a route card dated in pencil. A character or place must make a decision under uncertainty that can later be observed in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Arrival Evidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author locations, characters, tasks, rewards, costs, refusal routes, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcomes, physical clues, and delayed callbacks. The side quest begins with a concrete disturbance rather than a generic fetch request. Give each named person a practical limit and each place a material detail. Branches must alter a reachable owner state or projection. Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Arrival Evidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scale, contrast, non-color cues, reduced motion, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, batching, pagination, lazy loading, and safe degradation. Exercise long localization, repeated refresh, missing references, empty catalogs, stale rows, and high-volume records. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, save delta, and first-page latency. The player can cancel, defer, and recover without relying on a single sensory channel or a hidden timeout.

**Arrival Evidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum impact, null semantics, and deletion behavior. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and content correction. Stable ordering cannot depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A stateless projection must reproduce exactly; a durable change must name capture, restore, migration, and rollback.

**Arrival Evidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, data validation, Core or owner contract, event wiring, host route, content sample, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Use focused evidence for the smallest affected region; do not treat a compile result as runtime integration. Record exact files, owner claims, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Documentation volume never promotes a proposal. Rollout begins with a representative sample and expands only after the owner, consumer, persistence, and determinism receipts pass.

**Arrival Evidence Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Continuation Wave 16 — Plan 5 — Regional Supply And Travel

Wave 16 adds a fresh, owner-bound expansion layer for **regional supply and travel**. It is a planning scaffold only. The current 30-field structure remains active; these passes add new playable seams, high-volume authoring, story callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **route, cargo, settlement, weather, vehicle, communications, and expedition owners**. Material anchors include **a bell at the gate, a shared water can, a driver’s chalk mark, and a route card signed after dusk**. Observable markers include **arrival confidence, sharing window, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and appeal history**.

### Pass 155 — Arrival Timestamp Cards

This pass tests how **arrival timestamp cards** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over route, cargo, settlement, weather, vehicle, communications, and expedition owners; it does not add a second regional supply and travel authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Arrival Timestamp Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees arrival confidence, sharing window, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and appeal history with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Arrival Timestamp Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Arrival Timestamp Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Arrival Timestamp Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present arrival confidence, sharing window, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and appeal history as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Arrival Timestamp Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross arrival confidence, sharing window, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and appeal history with the material anchors a bell at the gate, a shared water can, a driver’s chalk mark, and a route card signed after dusk. A character or place must make a decision under uncertainty that can later be observed in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Arrival Timestamp Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author locations, characters, tasks, rewards, costs, refusal routes, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcomes, physical clues, and delayed callbacks. The side quest begins with a concrete disturbance rather than a generic fetch request. Give each named person a practical limit and each place a material detail. Branches must alter a reachable owner state or projection. Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Arrival Timestamp Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scale, contrast, non-color cues, reduced motion, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, batching, pagination, lazy loading, and safe degradation. **Arrival Timestamp Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

Capture only durable facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Stable ordering cannot depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A stateless projection must reproduce exactly; a durable change must name capture, restore, migration, and rollback.

**Arrival Timestamp Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Wave 16 high-volume content and story bank — Regional Supply And Travel

This bank expands **regional supply and travel** through the existing **route, cargo, settlement, weather, vehicle, communications, and expedition owners**. It is authored content and verification scaffolding, not a second authority. Every row carries a stable snake_case ID, schema version, source reference, lifecycle status, localization key, owner, and rollback note. The bank is exercised against **arrival confidence, sharing window, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and appeal history** and uses **a bell at the gate, a shared water can, a driver’s chalk mark, and a route card signed after dusk** as material evidence.

### High-volume field 1 — Timestamp evidence families

The **timestamp evidence families** field covers **timestamp, confidence, sample, hold, evidence, release, and refusal**. Start with a representative sample, validate it through the current loader and catalog integrity path, then expand by bounded pages. Reject duplicate IDs, unresolved references, unsupported effects, contradictory lifecycle values, and rows with no reachable consumer. Each row states whether it is authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state; a mutable result stays with its canonical owner.

For play, begin with an observable disturbance and offer verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved results. At least one row crosses three existing domains and changes a visible route, relationship boundary, room condition, map confidence, archive entry, or expedition timing. The callback names its publisher, consumer, consequence owner, and source age.

The host supports pagination, filtering, loading, empty, stale, redacted, and error states. Long localization wraps, focus survives refresh, and uncertainty is written rather than encoded by color. ## Wave 16 compact integration and acceptance packet — Regional Supply And Travel

The wave remains a documentation-only proposal over **timestamp evidence and appeals**. Before implementation, verify owner, consumer, route, save, replay, accessibility, performance, and rollback. The high-volume bank must pass a representative sample before expansion. Story branches must change a reachable owner state or projection and retain a coherent refusal path. Any missing seam, duplicate authority, unowned mechanic, or contradictory save contract stops the packet and returns it to premise review.

**Five-point handoff:** (1) current-source premise and collision search; (2) one owner and one event/save seam; (3) data, localization, migration, and validator evidence; (4) player route, side-quest callback, replay, accessibility, and performance evidence; (5) exact files, focused verification, limitations, rollback, and next audit.

## Continuation Wave 17 — Plan 5 — Regional Supply And Travel

Wave 17 adds a fresh, owner-bound expansion layer for **regional supply and travel**. It is a planning scaffold only. The current 30-field structure remains active; these passes add new playable seams, high-volume authoring, story callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **route, cargo, settlement, weather, vehicle, communications, and expedition owners**. Material anchors include **a bell at the gate, a folded tarp, a driver’s two-finger signal, and a route card initialed at dawn**. Observable markers include **arrival confidence, sharing window, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and review history**.

### Pass 166 — Arrival Confirmation Notes

This pass tests how **arrival confirmation notes** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over route, cargo, settlement, weather, vehicle, communications, and expedition owners; it does not add a second regional supply and travel authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Arrival Confirmation Notes receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees arrival confidence, sharing window, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and review history with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Arrival Confirmation Notes receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Arrival Confirmation Notes receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Arrival Confirmation Notes receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present arrival confidence, sharing window, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and review history as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Arrival Confirmation Notes receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross arrival confidence, sharing window, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and review history with the material anchors a bell at the gate, a folded tarp, a driver’s two-finger signal, and a route card initialed at dawn. A character or place must make a decision under uncertainty that can later be observed in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Arrival Confirmation Notes receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author locations, characters, tasks, rewards, costs, refusal routes, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcomes, physical clues, and delayed callbacks. The side quest begins with a concrete disturbance rather than a generic fetch request. Give each named person a practical limit and each place a material detail. Branches must alter a reachable owner state or projection. Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Arrival Confirmation Notes receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scale, contrast, non-color cues, reduced motion, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, batching, pagination, lazy loading, and safe degradation. Exercise long localization, repeated refresh, missing references, empty catalogs, stale rows, and high-volume records. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, save delta, and first-page latency. **Arrival Confirmation Notes receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Stable ordering cannot depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A stateless projection must reproduce exactly; a durable change must name capture, restore, migration, and rollback.

**Arrival Confirmation Notes receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

Sequence premise audit, data validation, Core or owner contract, event wiring, host route, content sample, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. **Arrival Confirmation Notes receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Wave 18 narrative and side-quest dossier — Regional Supply And Travel

### Story packet 1 — The Lantern Witness

A practical disturbance makes **the lantern witness** matter. The player can verify, accept, defer, share, or refuse. A person or place bears a material clue from **a lantern at weigh-in, a rope coiled on the hood, a driver’s open notebook, and a route card with two signatures**; the clue returns later in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Quiet success protects a routine, costly success spends a real resource, and unresolved play leaves an honest unknown. The receipt names the owner command, durable consequence, migration behavior, deterministic ordering, callback, and rollback.

## Wave 18 compact integration and acceptance packet — Regional Supply And Travel

The wave remains a documentation-only proposal over **witness evidence and commons**. Before implementation, verify owner, consumer, route, save, replay, accessibility, performance, and rollback. The high-volume bank must pass a representative sample before expansion. Story branches must change a reachable owner state or projection and retain a coherent refusal path. Any missing seam, duplicate authority, unowned mechanic, or contradictory save contract stops the packet and returns it to premise review.

**Five-point handoff:** (1) current-source premise and collision search; (2) one owner and one event/save seam; (3) data, localization, migration, and validator evidence; (4) player route, side-quest callback, replay, accessibility, and performance evidence; (5) exact files, focused verification, limitations, rollback, and next audit.

## Continuation Wave 19 — Plan 5 — Regional Supply And Travel

Wave 19 adds a fresh, owner-bound expansion layer for **regional supply and travel**. It is a planning scaffold only. The current 30-field structure remains active; these passes add new playable seams, high-volume authoring, story callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **route, cargo, settlement, weather, vehicle, communications, and expedition owners**. Material anchors include **a gate bell rung twice, a rope beside the scale, a notebook with one correction, and a route card carrying three initials**. Observable markers include **arrival confidence, shared load, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and audit status**.

### Pass 188 — Arrival Witness Review

This pass tests how **arrival witness review** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over route, cargo, settlement, weather, vehicle, communications, and expedition owners; it does not add a second regional supply and travel authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Arrival Witness Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees arrival confidence, shared load, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and audit status with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Arrival Witness Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Arrival Witness Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Arrival Witness Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present arrival confidence, shared load, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and audit status as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Arrival Witness Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross arrival confidence, shared load, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and audit status with the material anchors a gate bell rung twice, a rope beside the scale, a notebook with one correction, and a route card carrying three initials. A character or place must make a decision under uncertainty that can later be observed in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Arrival Witness Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author locations, characters, tasks, rewards, costs, refusal routes, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcomes, physical clues, and delayed callbacks. The side quest begins with a concrete disturbance rather than a generic fetch request. Give each named person a practical limit and each place a material detail. Branches must alter a reachable owner state or projection. Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Arrival Witness Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scale, contrast, non-color cues, reduced motion, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, batching, pagination, lazy loading, and safe degradation. Exercise long localization, repeated refresh, missing references, empty catalogs, stale rows, and high-volume records. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, save delta, and first-page latency. The player can cancel, defer, and recover without relying on a single sensory channel or a hidden timeout.

**Arrival Witness Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum impact, null semantics, and deletion behavior. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and content correction. Stable ordering cannot depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A stateless projection must reproduce exactly; a durable change must name capture, restore, migration, and rollback.

**Arrival Witness Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, data validation, Core or owner contract, event wiring, host route, content sample, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Use focused evidence for the smallest affected region; do not treat a compile result as runtime integration. Record exact files, owner claims, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Documentation volume never promotes a proposal. Rollout begins with a representative sample and expands only after the owner, consumer, persistence, and determinism receipts pass.

**Arrival Witness Review receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Continuation Wave 20 — Plan 5 — Regional Supply And Travel

Wave 20 adds a fresh, owner-bound expansion layer for **regional supply and travel**. It is a planning scaffold only. The current 30-field structure remains active; these passes add new playable seams, high-volume authoring, story callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **route, cargo, settlement, weather, vehicle, communications, and expedition owners**. Material anchors include **a lantern hung at the gate, a rope marked at the scale, a notebook with a red line, and a route card carrying four initials**. Observable markers include **arrival confidence, shared load, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and audit status**.

### Pass 199 — Arrival Audit Cards

This pass tests how **arrival audit cards** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over route, cargo, settlement, weather, vehicle, communications, and expedition owners; it does not add a second regional supply and travel authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Arrival Audit Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees arrival confidence, shared load, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and audit status with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Arrival Audit Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Arrival Audit Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Arrival Audit Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present arrival confidence, shared load, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and audit status as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Arrival Audit Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross arrival confidence, shared load, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and audit status with the material anchors a lantern hung at the gate, a rope marked at the scale, a notebook with a red line, and a route card carrying four initials. A character or place must make a decision under uncertainty that can later be observed in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Arrival Audit Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author locations, characters, tasks, rewards, costs, refusal routes, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcomes, physical clues, and delayed callbacks. The side quest begins with a concrete disturbance rather than a generic fetch request. Give each named person a practical limit and each place a material detail. Branches must alter a reachable owner state or projection. Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Arrival Audit Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scale, contrast, non-color cues, reduced motion, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, batching, pagination, lazy loading, and safe degradation. Exercise long localization, repeated refresh, missing references, empty catalogs, stale rows, and high-volume records. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, save delta, and first-page latency. The player can cancel, defer, and recover without relying on a single sensory channel or a hidden timeout.

**Arrival Audit Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum impact, null semantics, and deletion behavior. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and content correction. Stable ordering cannot depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A stateless projection must reproduce exactly; a durable change must name capture, restore, migration, and rollback.

**Arrival Audit Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, data validation, Core or owner contract, event wiring, host route, content sample, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Use focused evidence for the smallest affected region; do not treat a compile result as runtime integration. Record exact files, owner claims, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Documentation volume never promotes a proposal. Rollout begins with a representative sample and expands only after the owner, consumer, persistence, and determinism receipts pass.

**Arrival Audit Cards receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

A person or place bears a material clue from **a gate lantern lit blue, a rope tied at the scale, a notebook with a marginal arrow, and a route card carrying four initials**; the clue returns later in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Quiet success protects a routine, costly success spends a real resource, and unresolved play leaves an honest unknown. The receipt names the owner command, durable consequence, migration behavior, deterministic ordering, callback, and rollback.

## Wave 21 compact integration and acceptance packet — Regional Supply And Travel

The wave remains a documentation-only proposal over **signature audit and commons**. Before implementation, verify owner, consumer, route, save, replay, accessibility, performance, and rollback. The high-volume bank must pass a representative sample before expansion. Story branches must change a reachable owner state or projection and retain a coherent refusal path. Any missing seam, duplicate authority, unowned mechanic, or contradictory save contract stops the packet and returns it to premise review.

**Five-point handoff:** (1) current-source premise and collision search; (2) one owner and one event/save seam; (3) data, localization, migration, and validator evidence; (4) player route, side-quest callback, replay, accessibility, and performance evidence; (5) exact files, focused verification, limitations, rollback, and next audit.

## Continuation Wave 22 — Plan 5 — Regional Supply And Travel

Wave 22 adds a fresh, owner-bound expansion layer for **regional supply and travel**. It is a planning scaffold only. The current 30-field structure remains active; these passes add new playable seams, high-volume authoring, story callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **route, cargo, settlement, weather, vehicle, communications, and expedition owners**. Material anchors include **a blue flag on the gate, a rope with one knot, a notebook with a margin triangle, and a route card carrying four initials**. Observable markers include **arrival confidence, shared load, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and review status**.

### Pass 221 — Arrival Signal Records

This pass tests how **arrival signal records** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over route, cargo, settlement, weather, vehicle, communications, and expedition owners; it does not add a second regional supply and travel authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Arrival Signal Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees arrival confidence, shared load, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and review status with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Arrival Signal Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Arrival Signal Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Arrival Signal Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present arrival confidence, shared load, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and review status as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Arrival Signal Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross arrival confidence, shared load, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and review status with the material anchors a blue flag on the gate, a rope with one knot, a notebook with a margin triangle, and a route card carrying four initials. A character or place must make a decision under uncertainty that can later be observed in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Arrival Signal Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author locations, characters, tasks, rewards, costs, refusal routes, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcomes, physical clues, and delayed callbacks. The side quest begins with a concrete disturbance rather than a generic fetch request. Give each named person a practical limit and each place a material detail. Branches must alter a reachable owner state or projection. Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Arrival Signal Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scale, contrast, non-color cues, reduced motion, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, batching, pagination, lazy loading, and safe degradation. Exercise long localization, repeated refresh, missing references, empty catalogs, stale rows, and high-volume records. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, save delta, and first-page latency. The player can cancel, defer, and recover without relying on a single sensory channel or a hidden timeout.

**Arrival Signal Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum impact, null semantics, and deletion behavior. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and content correction. Stable ordering cannot depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A stateless projection must reproduce exactly; a durable change must name capture, restore, migration, and rollback.

**Arrival Signal Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, data validation, Core or owner contract, event wiring, host route, content sample, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Use focused evidence for the smallest affected region; do not treat a compile result as runtime integration. Record exact files, owner claims, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Documentation volume never promotes a proposal. Rollout begins with a representative sample and expands only after the owner, consumer, persistence, and determinism receipts pass.

**Arrival Signal Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

The proposal is a bounded extension over route, cargo, settlement, weather, vehicle, communications, and expedition owners; it does not add a second regional supply and travel authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Crossing Fallback Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees arrival confidence, shared load, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and review status with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Crossing Fallback Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Crossing Fallback Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Crossing Fallback Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present arrival confidence, shared load, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and review status as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Crossing Fallback Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross arrival confidence, shared load, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and review status with the material anchors a blue flag on the gate, a rope with one knot, a notebook with a margin triangle, and a route card carrying four initials. A character or place must make a decision under uncertainty that can later be observed in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Crossing Fallback Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author locations, characters, tasks, rewards, costs, refusal routes, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcomes, physical clues, and delayed callbacks. The side quest begins with a concrete disturbance rather than a generic fetch request. Give each named person a practical limit and each place a material detail. Branches must alter a reachable owner state or projection. Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Crossing Fallback Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scale, contrast, non-color cues, reduced motion, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, batching, pagination, lazy loading, and safe degradation. Exercise long localization, repeated refresh, missing references, empty catalogs, stale rows, and high-volume records. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, save delta, and first-page latency. The player can cancel, defer, and recover without relying on a single sensory channel or a hidden timeout.

**Crossing Fallback Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum impact, null semantics, and deletion behavior. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and content correction. Stable ordering cannot depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A stateless projection must reproduce exactly; a durable change must name capture, restore, migration, and rollback.

**Crossing Fallback Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, data validation, Core or owner contract, event wiring, host route, content sample, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Use focused evidence for the smallest affected region; do not treat a compile result as runtime integration. Record exact files, owner claims, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Documentation volume never promotes a proposal. Rollout begins with a representative sample and expands only after the owner, consumer, persistence, and determinism receipts pass.

**Crossing Fallback Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Wave 22 high-volume content and story bank — Regional Supply And Travel

This bank expands **regional supply and travel** through the existing **route, cargo, settlement, weather, vehicle, communications, and expedition owners**. It is authored content and verification scaffolding, not a second authority. Every row carries a stable snake_case ID, schema version, source reference, lifecycle status, localization key, owner, and rollback note. The bank is exercised against **arrival confidence, shared load, demand age, recovery time, permit condition, and audit status** and uses **a blue flag on the gate, a rope with one knot, a notebook with a margin triangle, and a route card carrying four initials** as material evidence.

### High-volume field 1 — Signal audit families

The **signal audit families** field covers **signal, confidence, sample, hold, evidence, release, and refusal**. Start with a representative sample, validate it through the current loader and catalog integrity path, then expand by bounded pages. Reject duplicate IDs, unresolved references, unsupported effects, contradictory lifecycle values, and rows with no reachable consumer. Each row states whether it is authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state; a mutable result stays with its canonical owner.

For play, begin with an observable disturbance and offer verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved results. At least one row crosses three existing domains and changes a visible route, relationship boundary, room condition, map confidence, archive entry, or expedition timing. The callback names its publisher, consumer, consequence owner, and source age.

The host supports pagination, filtering, loading, empty, stale, redacted, and error states. Long localization wraps, focus survives refresh, and uncertainty is written rather than encoded by color. Measure first-page latency, allocations, event fan-out, save delta, and safe degradation. A deterministic fixture repeats the same seed and ordered inputs after save and reload. The receipt records source paths, owner evidence, unresolved collisions, migration behavior, rollback, and the stop line if the premise fails.

**Field receipt:** sample IDs; owner API; source references; state ladder; side-quest hook; localization keys; pagination budget; replay fixture; rollback path.
